idiom_name: small behaviour interfaces held in a slice; struct embedding for the fixed case
implementation_notes: Go has no inheritance to escape, so the pattern needs no base class: a component is any type implementing a narrow interface (type Updater interface { Update(dt float64) }) and the entity is a struct holding parts []Updater or explicit named fields, which makes pluggable behaviour ordinary interface use rather than a designed structure. When the capability set is fixed, anonymous-field embedding expresses the same has-a reuse with no dynamic list at all (type Player struct { Physics; Renderer }) and is the form to prefer; a heterogeneous bag keyed by reflect.Type reproduces the ECS-style lookup but pays reflection and loses compile-time safety, so reserve it - or a generics-based ECS such as donburi - for genuinely data-driven entity sets.
pitfalls: A []Updater slice boxes every component behind an interface value, so a hot loop over thousands of entities should store concrete types (or use a generics-based ECS) instead of chasing interfaces.
Embedding promotes methods onto the entity: two embedded components with the same method name make the method ambiguous, and the entity silently stops satisfying the interface you expected.
An embedded struct's methods receive the embedded value, not the entity, so a component that needs the entity's other fields must be a named pointer field with explicit forwarding.
